chapter: Berlin and the Turner and Bryant bands
title: Berlin cabaret in 1933: Annie Goudy and Mack the Knife
summary: Back on Berlin, he describes the Feminina with seven bands and singer Annie Goudy singing Mack the Knife, in a style he thinks influenced Piaf, plus Marlene Dietrich or Lotte Lenya.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: (Inaudible). So getting back to Berlin, the place, as I said, place called Feminina. And they had a woman singing, Annie Gordy --
How did she spell her name?

Let's see, G-o-u-d-y. She was singing "Funf Pfenig Opera," or "Mack the Knife." This is 1933, '34. And she was singing, she was a blues singer, somewhere. And that's where Edith Piaf got her style, I believe. And she Little person. would swing and sing it. /And I never forgot that.
Then they also had a singer, "Falling in Love Again," I don't know if it was Marlene Dietrich there or not, but I
know they were singing that song at that time, in that cabaret. Because you had seven bands.
It might have been Lotte Lenya (PHONETIC). Did you meet her during those years?
